subject: Question about audit file ID and request for current SOC 2 Type II
messages:
From: Liam Ortiz <liam.ortiz@atlaspay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@atlaspay.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: SOC 2 file ID mismatch during vendor intake

Hi Evelyn,

We're finalizing the vendor review for Redwood and hit a small snag with the SOC 2 you submitted. The PDF in our intake system shows an audit identifier 'SOC2-2024-10-RED-82' in the cover metadata, but the link in your shared attestations page references 'attest-RED-202410' (our intake team treats those as different records).

Could you please:
- Confirm which report is the canonical current Type II for Redwood (cover dates and audit ID), and
- Provide the preferred downloadable file (PDF) and any bridge/interim attestation if the audit window doesn't fully cover our contract effective date (Sept 1).

We also need an evidence index (mapping of controls to evidence artifacts) to satisfy our InfoSec reviewer — a CSV or short spreadsheet is fine.

Thanks,
Liam

--
Liam Ortiz
Senior Vendor Analyst
AtlasPay Procurement
liam.ortiz@atlaspay.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam Ortiz <liam.ortiz@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 file ID mismatch during vendor intake

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the confusion.

Short answer: the canonical, signed SOC 2 Type II covers Oct 1, 2023 — Sep 30, 2024 and is published as Redwood_SOC2_v2024-10.pdf. Our public attestations portal and the internal file ID use slightly different naming conventions; that likely explains the mismatch.

Actions I will take now:
- Attach the canonical PDF export directly to this thread (see attachment stub below).
- Attach our bridge letter that explains coverage for Oct 2024 — Aug 2025 (interim coverage we issued for renewal gaps).
- Attach a simple evidence index CSV that maps key controls to evidence artifacts.

Marcus (Head of Information Security) — looping you in to confirm the audit identifier equivalence and to confirm whether the bridge letter is sufficient for AtlasPay's contract start date.

I should have everything to you by EOD tomorrow. If you have a preferred file ID that you need on the PDF metadata (our compliance portal supports setting a reference tag), I can update the PDF metadata before sending.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Manager, Compliance & Customer Trust
Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com]

[Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_v2024-10.pdf (PDF, 2.3MB) — canonical Type II report]
[Attachment: SOC2_bridge_letter_Q1-2026.pdf (PDF, 48KB) — interim coverage letter]
[Attachment: evidence_index.csv (CSV, 12KB)]
From: Liam Ortiz <liam.ortiz@atlaspay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SOC 2 file ID mismatch during vendor intake

Hi Evelyn,

Appreciate the quick response and the attachments — the portal accepted the PDF but our intake still flagged the file-level ID in the PDF metadata as different from the audit record ID in the attestations portal URL. We can accept either as long as you confirm equivalence in writing (simple statement that 'SOC2-2024-10-RED-82' == 'attest-RED-202410' and that both point to the attached file).

Two small asks from InfoSec:
- Can Marcus confirm the bridge letter explicitly states the audit window coverage and the controls that remained in place during the interim period?
- Can you add a one-line statement on the PDF cover metadata (or on a short letter) with the audit record ID AtlasPay should reference?

If it's easier, a one-page attestation PDF with the matching ID and a DocuSign signature would cut through procurement. We can share a DocuSign room if helpful.

Thanks — target is to finish vendor approval by Aug 25 so the contract can begin Sept 1.

Liam
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam Ortiz <liam.ortiz@atlaspay.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 file ID mismatch during vendor intake

Hi Liam — thanks for the note and deadline callout. Quick confirmation:

1) Equivalence: 'SOC2-2024-10-RED-82' (internal audit identifier) and 'attest-RED-202410' (portal record) both reference the same signed Type II report covering 2023-10-01 through 2024-09-30. We confirm that they are equivalent identifiers for procurement reference.

2) Bridge coverage: the attached bridge letter (SOC2_bridge_letter_Q1-2026.pdf) explicitly states that controls were maintained and monitored between 2024-10-01 and 2025-08-31 and indicates the scope limitations (no new control scope additions). That language should satisfy a standard interim attestation. If you need more granular control-by-control affirmations, we can provide the evidence_index.csv mapping which includes artifact sources and timestamps.

3) DocuSign attestation: happy to sign a one-page attestation with the AtlasPay file ID. If you send a DocuSign room link we will sign it and ensure the attestation PDF contains the requested audit record ID in the cover metadata.

Let me know the DocuSign URL and the exact string you prefer on the cover.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Information Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2_bridge_letter_Q1-2026.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]
